subject: Scheduling: Dedicated capacity sizing call / throughput & latency

Subject: Quick recap + next step: dedicated capacity sizing call

Adam / Priya — great conversation today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

- Primary use case: real-time chat assistant embedded in support product (customer-facing).
- Expected peak traffic: TBD from your side; we discussed bursty patterns driven by events.
- Latency target: 200ms p95 for user-facing responses (you mentioned 150–250ms as the goal).
- Models: planning to evaluate a mix of open LLMs (gpt-3.5-like and a 70B variant) — accuracy vs cost tradeoffs.
- Data security: you need VPC/private deployment for PII handling; discussed Dedicated or Private options.

Next step: schedule a dedicated capacity sizing call (technical deep dive) so our SE can size GPU pools and recommend batching/KV-cache settings. On that call we typically cover: throughput targets (peak QPS), average tokens per request, context length, sequence length distribution, model variant choices, and any latency SLOs you must meet.

Proposed slots (PST):
- Wed Mar 3, 10:00–10:45 AM PST
- Thu Mar 4, 2:00–2:45 PM PST

If neither works, please share 2–3 times that do. I've attached a one-page mutual action plan and a short RFI template — if you can fill the RFI before the call it speeds the sizing exercise.

Attachments: MAP_Acme_AI_v1.pdf, RFI_Acme_AI_request_for_info.xlsx

Thanks — looping in Mateo (SE) and Monica (CS) to join the sizing call.

—
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Quick recap + next step: dedicated capacity sizing call

Marissa — thanks for the recap and the materials. Wed/Thu both look possible but prefer Thu if that helps. A few quick data points to help size before the call: 

- Expected peak (initial rollout): ~120 concurrent QA sessions, translating to ~80 QPS at peak for inference.
- Average tokens per request: ~350 tokens in + ~70 tokens out (we typically truncate to 512 total).
- Typical context length: 1–2 KB of prompt (mainly recent conversation + retrieval snippets).
- Models: we'll test two model families — a 30B quantized model and a higher-cost 70B variant for high-quality responses.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 200ms is the goal; p50 should be <80ms where possible.

Happy to share anonymized sample traffic (headers + token counts) — I'll upload to the Drive link you provided if that works.

Priya will coordinate calendars on our side. For now please book Thu Mar 4, 2:00–2:45 PM PST if that slot is still free.

Thanks,
Adam
CEO, Acme AI
adam@acme.ai | (617) 555-0101
